questions.question: Front tires must have a tread depth of ____ in every major groove.
questions.correctAnswerText: 4/32 of an inch
questions.explanation: Commercial vehicles need a tread depth of 4/32 of an inch in every major groove on front tires. Other tires need a tread depth of 2/32 of an inch.

questions.question: Why do large vehicles use air brakes?

options.text: Other brake systems are too loud.
Other brake systems are hard to find.

questions.correctAnswerText: Air brakes work very well.
questions.explanation: When used and maintained correctly, air brakes are safe and work well for stopping large, heavy vehicles.

questions.question: How do you check for a leak in hydraulic brakes?

options.text: Pump the brake pedal three times. Hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
Press the brake pedal down hard and release it. If it does not return to normal, there may be a problem.
Press the brake pedal down hard and release it. If the brakes squeak, there may be a problem.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pump the brake pedal three times. Hold it down for five seconds. If the pedal moves, there may be a problem.
questions.explanation: To check hydraulic brakes, pump the pedal three times. Then press the pedal firmly for five seconds. The pedal should not move. If it does, there may be a leak or another brake system problem.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It takes your mind and hands off driving.
A message might upset the driver.
Drivers may focus too much on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It takes your mind and hands off driving.
questions.explanation: Texting while driving is dangerous because it distracts your mind from the road and requires you to remove at least one hand from the steering wheel.

questions.question: While driving, a driver should:

options.text: Not worry about what is happening on the sides of the vehicle.
Watch what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
Not worry about what is happening behind the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch what is happening on all sides of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: You must be aware of what is happening on all sides of your vehicle at all times. Look ahead and check your mirrors on both sides regularly while driving.

questions.question: Vehicles with low underneath clearance may be difficult to drive:
questions.correctAnswerText: Over railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: It can be hard to cross railroad tracks when pulling a trailer with low clearance. Trailers that sit low and single-axle tractors pulling long trailers are especially difficult to drive over raised crossings.

questions.question: Glad hands should be securely connected to:
questions.correctAnswerText: The correct air lines.
questions.explanation: When checking the converter dolly, make sure all parts are present and working correctly. Air lines must be firmly attached to the correct glad hands with no leaks. They should have enough slack to allow easy turning.

questions.question: If you unlock the pintle hook without pulling the dolly out from under the rear trailer:

options.text: The tow bar may fly up.

questions.correctAnswerText: The tow bar may fly up.
questions.explanation: Never unlock the pintle hook while the dolly is still under the rear trailer. The dolly tow bar could fly up and cause serious injury.

questions.question: If a vehicle's Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) is not working:

options.text: The vehicle will have no brakes.
The vehicle will still be able to brake.
The vehicle will likely travel faster than usual.

questions.correctAnswerText: The vehicle will still be able to brake.
questions.explanation: The ABS helps prevent wheel lockup by reducing brake pressure. If the ABS is not working, the vehicle's normal brakes still work. Drive and brake as you normally would.

questions.question: You can test a tractor protection valve by:

options.text: Opening all of the vehicle's shut-off valves.
Releasing air with the brake pedal and waiting for the emergency signal to activate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Releasing air with the brake pedal and waiting for the emergency signal to activate.
questions.explanation: To test the tractor protection valve, let the air supply charge fully. Turn off the engine. Then release air by pressing the brake pedal several times. The valve should activate its emergency position when air pressure drops to an unsafe level.

questions.question: When starting down a hill, you should switch into a ____ gear.
questions.correctAnswerText: Lower
questions.explanation: Switch to a low gear before going down a hill. Gravity will make your vehicle go faster as it goes downhill.

questions.question: A driver should use the trailer hand valve to:
questions.correctAnswerText: Test the trailer brakes.
questions.explanation: Using the trailer hand valve while driving can cause a skid. Use it only to test the trailer brakes.

questions.question: During a trip, gauges are:

options.text: The only way a driver can learn of potential trouble with the vehicle.
A way to learn of potential trouble with the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: A way to learn of potential trouble with the vehicle.
questions.explanation: During a trip, check the gauges, mirrors, tires, cargo, and lights regularly for signs of trouble.

questions.question: If you see a distracted driver ahead, you should:

options.text: Maintain a safe distance from the vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Maintain a safe distance from the vehicle.
questions.explanation: If you see a distracted driver, stay far away and keep a safe following distance.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a cause of hydraulic brake failure?
questions.correctAnswerText: Downshifting
questions.explanation: Hydraulic brake failure usually comes from loss of hydraulic pressure or overuse on long hills, which causes brake fade.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a recommended way to spot trouble?

options.text: Checking critical items only at the beginning and end of a trip

questions.correctAnswerText: Checking critical items only at the beginning and end of a trip
questions.explanation: Check your vehicle regularly during a trip. Watch the gauges, check mirrors, and look at tires, cargo, and lights. Use all your senses to catch early signs of trouble.

questions.question: Roads are especially slippery when rain first starts because:

options.text: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
The water has nowhere to go.

questions.correctAnswerText: The fresh rain mixes with oil on the roadway.
questions.explanation: At the start of rain, water mixes with oil that has dripped onto the road. This mixture is very slippery.

questions.question: If you use the trailer hand brake while your trailer is skidding, it will:
questions.correctAnswerText: Continue the skid.
questions.explanation: If your trailer is skidding, release the brakes to help your tires grip the road. Using the trailer hand brake during a skid will make the skid continue.

questions.question: When backing up with a trailer, you should start by:

options.text: Turning the steering wheel in the direction of the turn.
Turning the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the turn.
Turning the wheel as sharply as possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turning the steering wheel in the direction opposite of the turn.
questions.explanation: When backing with a trailer, turn the steering wheel opposite to the direction you want the trailer to go. Once the trailer starts to turn, reverse the steering wheel direction to follow it.

questions.question: What does a vehicle inspection report do?

options.text: Inform the motor carrier about problems that may need fixing
Ensure that the vehicle is inspected regularly
Keep people accountable for inspecting the vehicle

questions.correctAnswerText: Inform the motor carrier about problems that may need fixing
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report tells the carrier what problems need to be fixed.
